doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The YMCA band, Haughton's lessons and Sousa marches
summary: Johnson played in the Senate Avenue YMCA band, took Sunday trombone lessons from Haughton, and enjoyed Sousa marches.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Let me ask you about something at the same time. I played in the YMCA band, and I remember running across music with your name written across the top so it evidently had been your part. I'm wondering if you remember much about the Senate Avenue band [the YMCA was located on Senate Avenue] because I remember the little man who played the trombone, and he used to tell me that you sat up under him for quite some time in that band.

That was a wonderful period in my life as far as getting my feet wet in the domain of music. It was the YMCA band. I looked forward to going to those rehearsals and playing all those wonderful Sousa marches. It was really important and exciting, and I couldn’t get enough of it. Yes, the guy who was the lead trombone player, I think his name was Haughton.
Charlie Haughton, I believe. Charlie Haughton, a wonderful trombonist who, in a manner of speaking, took me under his wing in that I would go to his house on

Sunday afternoons and take a lesson from him. I looked forward to going to his home on Sunday afternoons taking lessons, trombone lessons. I looked forward to going to the rehearsals where we played all these fantastic Sousa marches. Stars and Stripes Forever is one that comes to my mind. There were a zillion of them. That’s the only one I can think of. I know David [Baker] appreciates the fact that these Sousa marches always had interesting trombone parts. It was contrapuntal to the rest of whatever the orchestra was doing. They always had something else to do, and it was just wonderful.
I tell you, it was such a thrill to see your name written at the top of those parts, 'cause then everybody fought to try to get the part that J.J. had played.
[laughs]. I have fond memories of playing with the YMCA band.
How often did the YMCA band rehearse?
My best recollection is a couple of times a month, something like that. Yeah, on average, I’d say about twice a month.

All of the members had day jobs doing something else, so this was their passion on the side. What they did for their enjoyment was to get together and play in the YMCA band. But they all worked in the post office or for the government or in some plant or [at] Eli Lilly or whatever – [at the Army] Finance Center or what have you.
Did the YMCA band also perform?
Once in a great while they would perform at Douglas Park or at one of the other white parks] – not often, but now and again, yes.
